title: The Operational Facilitator may compress Root Edit timelines in an emergency, and may withhold the reason if disclosure would endanger Keel
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 permits the Operational Facilitator, "in an Urgent or Emergency Situation, as defined by the Sky Core Atlas in A.1.9.1.1," to "allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above."

Two features matter more than the speed-up itself. First, Keel does not define its own emergency; it inherits the definition from the Core Atlas, so an Agent cannot widen its emergency powers by editing its own Artifact — the trigger lives upstream where the Artifact Edit Restrictions prevent Keel from touching it.

Second, the transparency obligation is deliberately weak: "where feasible, the Operational Facilitator should announce the decision... and provide their reasoning via a public Sky Forum post... unless doing so would endanger Keel or its users." That is *should*, not must, qualified twice.

The suppressed detail is what exactly gets compressed. The routine path contains a 7-day review and a 3-day poll; the clause authorizes shortening "the timeline" without specifying a floor, so in principle both deliberation windows can shrink toward zero while the Facilitator's veto and execution roles remain intact. Emergency powers here concentrate what was already concentrated, and the check that survives is the ex-post record rather than any ex-ante limit.
description: Emergency Root Edits use the Atlas's own definition of Urgent/Emergency Situations and carry only a 'where feasible' duty to announce, making transparency the first thing sacrificed under time
